storage.title: Integrated wind–solar–hydrogen energy storage
storage.subtitle: Northwest China’s wind and solar bases can store off-peak surplus as hydrogen, then return electricity through fuel cells when demand peaks.
storage.visualTitle: A connected renewable hydrogen storage system
storage.visualAlt: Conceptual energy landscape connecting wind turbines and solar panels to an electrolyzer, hydrogen storage tanks, a fuel cell and the power grid. The drawing explains a process and does not depict a verified operating facility.
storage.supplyFlow: Stored hydrogen → fuel cell → electricity to the grid
storage.impact: This pathway can help reduce renewable-energy curtailment.
storage.note: Process illustration · capacity and round-trip efficiency are not shown

distributed.title: Distributed hydrogen power generation
distributed.subtitle: Fuel-cell backup can support remote and critical sites when the normal electricity supply is interrupted.
distributed.chpFlow: Hydrogen → fuel cell / CHP → electricity + useful heat
distributed.chpTitle: Pilot hydrogen combined heat and power
distributed.chpNote: Community-scale pilot systems are being tested; these are separate from the three backup examples.

cofiring.title: Hydrogen co-firing in coal power plants
cofiring.subtitle: A small hydrogen input joins the coal-fired boiler process as a pathway to reduce carbon emissions from coal-based generation.
cofiring.diagramTitle: Conceptual coal and hydrogen co-firing process
cofiring.diagramAlt: Coal and a separate hydrogen supply feed a simplified boiler combustion zone. Heat makes steam, steam turns a turbine and generator, and electricity flows to the grid. No blending ratio or performance value is represented.
cofiring.objective: Objective: reduce carbon emissions from coal power generation
cofiring.caveat: The briefing material does not specify a hydrogen blend ratio or a quantified CO₂ reduction.
cofiring.processShort: Coal + a small hydrogen input → boiler → steam → turbine → electricity
